//: Deny-all, deliberately -- see app/src/services/firebaseSession.ts and
README.md's 'Why does the app never talk to Firebase directly?' section.
The app never authenticates to Firebase as a client at all any more: it
signs a message proving wallet ownership, trades it for this project's
own session token via /api/session/create, and every read/write from
then on goes through this project's own /api endpoints via the Admin
SDK, which bypasses these rules entirely -- same as the ESP32 meters'
legacy database secret.
This file used to be a detailed per-uid ACL (auth.uid == a wallet,
checked on every path) from when the app *did* sign in via Firebase
Anonymous Auth. That model was replaced, but this file was left as an
ACL that *looked* real and active while auth.uid was always null for
every real request -- meaning `auth != null` was already effectively
unreachable for actual traffic, but a security audit correctly flagged
it as a live risk anyway: if Anonymous Auth (or any other Firebase Auth
method) were ever re-enabled on the Firebase console for an unrelated
reason, every one of those `auth != null` reads -- the full
deviceToWallet map, every pendingDevices entry, the whole email
directory -- would become exploitable by anyone who signs in, with no
code change on this side required to trigger it. Deny-all removes that
latent risk instead of relying on Anonymous Auth staying off forever.
If a client SDK path is ever reintroduced, write real rules for it
then, scoped to whatever auth model exists at that point -- don't
resurrect this file's old per-uid shape without re-deriving it.
Exception: .indexOn below. That's not an access rule (the Admin SDK
bypasses .read/.write regardless), it's a query-planning requirement
the Realtime Database engine enforces on every orderByChild call no
matter which SDK issues it -- listNotifications() in app/api/data.ts
queries notifications/$wallet ordered by createdAt and needs this index
to not fail outright.
